character_sheet: A hostile giant mole: a 32x20x56 body with a shoulder block, a three-block head ending in a snout with a six-spoke nose star, two arms of an upper arm, a hand and four 13-long claws, two legs of the same build, a rump and a stub tail (MolenoidModel.java:104-287, 37 parts). 200 HP, 18 damage, 12 armour, speed 0.35 (EntityMolenoid.java:77-86). On a 1-in-4 tick it picks prey in a 12-block box - non-creative players, monsters and the attackable animals, never another mole (:141-142, :280-302) - seeing through dirt, sand and gravel with its own block ray (:315-358); within 6 blocks plus half the target's width it raises its attacking flag and, within 4, bites on a double dice for 18 with a knockback (:147-151, :115-130), else lobs one to four mole-dirt blocks onto the ground around the target (:152-156, :211-226); farther out it paths at 1.25 (:158), the flag dropped when it finds nothing (:161). It digs as it goes: a three-block column ahead is cleared every tick, up or down toward the prey (:199, :243-268), and mounds of mole dirt are kicked up behind it in proportion to its speed (:175-197); walls cannot hurt it (:107-113). It spawns in the dark at night above y 50 under three blocks of clear air, no other within 16 (:387-397; ModEntities.java:272-274). Read it as a mole: a crawling dig with the arm chains sweeping, the nose star turning, a frantic dig when it is on its prey.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (MolenoidRenderer.java:23; shadow 1.0, :25) on a 256x256 sheet (MolenoidModel.java:289), molenoid.png (MolenoidRenderer.java:18); the hitbox is 3.9 x 2.6 (ModEntities.java:272-274). The original's ModelMolenoid(0.5f) argument was the wingspeed (MolenoidModel.java:21), not a scale. The arms and legs are position chains the code re-places each tick (hands 15 px along the arm, claws 10 px along the hand; :297-298, :300-301) - key the joints, not the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: y (and each chain's x / z positions)
groups.amplitude: arms and legs alike: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 at 1.3 x 0.5 = 0.65 rad/tick, 0 below the threshold; the arm or leg swings about ±0.628, the hand or foot 1.25x, the four claws or toes 1.5x about ∓0.174 (claws) / ∓0.261 (toes); each hand or foot is placed 15 px along its limb's yaw and each claw or toe set 10 px along the hand's or foot's; the legs take the negative of the arms' angle, and the same angle on both sides with mirrored rests puts left against right. The attacking branch: with the flag up the ARMS alone dig at 1.7 x 0.5 = 0.85 rad/tick and the full 45 deg, unscaled and with no threshold, while the legs keep the gait
groups.plain: the two arm chains and the two leg chains sweep about the vertical like a mole digging, each hand, foot, claw and toe set swinging farther than its limb, the legs against the arms and left against right; while the attacking flag is up the arms dig faster and even when it stands still
groups.math: g = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.3 * 0.5) * pi * 0.25 * amount : 0; a = attacking ? cos(t * 1.7 * 0.5) * pi * 0.25 : g; larm.yRot = a + 0.628; lhand.x/z = larm.x/z ± 15 along larm.yRot; lhand.yRot = a * 1.25; lclaw1..4.x/z = lhand.x/z ± 10 along lhand.yRot; lclaw1..4.yRot = a * 1.5 - 0.174; rarm.yRot = a - 0.628; rhand.yRot = a * 1.25; rclaw1..4.yRot = a * 1.5 + 0.174 (the right chain placed the mirror way); lleg.yRot = -g + 0.628; lfoot.yRot = -g * 1.25; ltoe1..4.yRot = -g * 1.5 - 0.261; rleg.yRot = -g - 0.628; rfoot.yRot = -g * 1.25; rtoe1..4.yRot = -g * 1.5 + 0.261; the feet and toes placed along the chain as the hands and claws are
groups.phase: the limbSwingAmount threshold of 0.1 gates the gait; the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (EntityMolenoid.java:51-52, set 1 within 6 blocks plus half the target's width on the 1-in-4 pass :147-148, 0 with no prey :161) selects the arms' unscaled dig over it; one gait group per rig is the generator's rule, so the arms and legs share this group
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 0.5 = 0.65 (a 9.67-tick period) for the gait, and x 1.7 x 0.5 = 0.85 (7.39 ticks) for the arms' attacking dig

groups.name: nose_star
groups.amplitude: pi = 3.14 rad (180 deg) each way about 0, the six spokes offset 0 / +30 / +60 / +90 / -60 / -30 deg — the star rocks through a full turn and back
groups.plain: the nose star rolls slowly back and forth through a full turn at all times
groups.math: s = cos(t * 0.1 * 0.5) * pi; nosestar1.zRot = s; nosestar2.zRot = s + 0.523; nosestar3.zRot = s + 1.047; nosestar4.zRot = s + 1.57; nosestar5.zRot = s - 1.047; nosestar6.zRot = s - 0.523
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.1 x 0.5 = 0.05: the natural period is 126 ticks (6.3 s)

behaviour: One gait rhythm above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 (MolenoidModel.java:295, :328-360): the arm and leg chains sweep 45 degrees x the walking speed about the vertical at 0.65 rad/tick, a 9.7-tick period, the hands and feet at 1.25 times the angle and the claws and toes at 1.5, each piece placed along the one before (15 and 10 px); the arms and legs take the same angle with opposite signs, so a left arm sweeps with the right leg - a crawling dig.

One branch on the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (EntityMolenoid.java:51-52), raised on the 1-in-4 pass within 6 blocks plus half the target's width (:147-148) and dropped when the pass finds no prey (:161): while it is up the arms dig at 0.85 rad/tick and full 45-degree amplitude whether or not the mole moves (:295), the legs still following the stride (:328).

The six-spoke nose star rolls through a full turn and back on a 126-tick cosine at all times (:361-366). The body, shoulders, the three head blocks, the rump and the tail are static; the head does not follow the look.

The bite (doHurtTarget, EntityMolenoid.java:115-130: 18 and a 0.8 knockback, within 4 blocks on the double dice :150-151), the block lob (:152-156, :211-226), the dig ahead (:243-268) and the spoil mounds (:175-197) are world edits on server rolls - no animation events today.
